provenance.note: no release point was supplied; the source sits at spill_fraction along the modeled reach
the elevation every node of the reach carries; the solver reads it as the channel's bathymetry
carrier discharge 2.2 m3/s (user-supplied)
Place name on the river, geocoded to the reach [supplied on this invocation]
Finite pulse injection window [supplied on this invocation]
Point-source discharge of the release itself, small against the river's carrier flow [supplied on this invocation]
Median grain diameter d50 of the bed - ~200 um fine sand, ~20 um silt, ~8 um mud (all modeled non-cohesive); read only when no gradation is given [supplied on this invocation]
Concentration of the marker tracer released at the source, which is what the deposited fraction is measured against [supplied on this invocation]
Modeled reach length downstream of the release; a longer reach is coarsened under the mesh node budget [supplied on this invocation]
Simulated physical time; the morphological factor is what makes a short window produce a readable bed change [supplied on this invocation]
Target element edge length the reach is triangulated at; scour depth is a resolution-bound class and a coarse mesh reads it low [supplied on this invocation]
Solve sizing class [declared constant default]
Along-reach release position, 0=upstream..1=downstream; the source must sit strictly INSIDE the reach, never on a boundary [declared scenario default]
Sustained wind driving a surface wind-stress term; 0 = no wind [declared scenario default]
Compass bearing the wind blows FROM (0=N, 90=E); only read when wind_speed_mps > 0 [declared scenario default]
Depth of the erodible sediment stock the bed can scour into [declared scenario default]
GAIA bed-load law: 1=Meyer-Peter-Mueller, 2=Einstein-Brown, 7=van Rijn [declared scenario default]
Amplifies bed change per hydraulic step so a short hydrograph yields a readable depth; a speed-up lever, not a rate [declared scenario default]
Arm the NESTOR channel-maintenance dig/dump rule on top of the mobile bed [declared scenario default]
Dredging rule: scheduled (remove a target volume over a window) | criterion (dig only where the bed silts within tolerance of grade) [declared scenario default]
Scheduled-mode target dredged volume [declared scenario default]
Criterion-mode siltation tolerance above the design grade [declared scenario default]
Criterion-mode dig target below the design grade [declared scenario default]
Also place the dug spoil in a downstream disposal zone [declared scenario default]

Bank setback the dig field is held back from the mapped water's edge, so the cut does not undercut the bank it is dug beside. It is also what excludes a stretch too narrow to dredge: narrower than twice the setback and no field survives there [declared scenario default]

not supplied; the coefficient is read as a Strickler one
